title: Generous fixed habit cap (or unlimited) — never change it
statement: A low or drifting free cap is the #1 monetization complaint; 'unlimited' also sells, so the level is a decision but the stability is not. Report 6: raising a 1-streak cap to 2 did not reduce complaints — the ask was unlimited — though the tone moved from 'scam' to 'love it, want more'. Report 7: a 4-habit cap held unchanged for 3½ years was still the top 2★ theme (0 of 27 complainers paid) while 11 users said 4 was plenty — stable is not enough if the level binds the 5–8-habit user. Report 11: 'First app that has more than 3 habits' was a reviewer's entire body — no cap was the acquisition wedge against the category, and whether it survived the paywall retrofit is unknown. Report 13: the free cap was cut from 5 to 3 in 2018 (the worst year, mean 2.85) and restored in 2020 without recovering the rating; 'hitting the cap while already engaged' is the one purchase trigger buyers name. Report 14: a 3-habit free cap drew its only 1★ free-tier complaint; the report's reading is that the cap must be generous enough to create the streak that creates the desire to pay. Report 16: a free tier of ONE habit drew 76 complaints at mean 2.22 ('a habit tracker that tracks one habit is not a habit tracker') and could not do trial work; 20 reviewers defended the earn-a-slot constraint at 3–6 habits (mean 4.60) — loved at 3–6, hated at 1. Report 20: 'unlimited habits, free' was the highest-mean theme in a 4,048-review corpus (54 explicit, mean 4.94) and the product's entire market position; capping it at 3 deleted the reason to exist — 63 reviews say exactly this, 99 complain about the cap, and 3 is below the threshold of usefulness (the report's defensible line is 7–10 free with paid depth elsewhere). Report 23 (a paid app, cap as design not paywall): raising the cap 6 → 12 → 24 cut complaints roughly in half each time and bought about three years; the request re-anchors on the new number and never falls below ~6%. Report 24 (counter-evidence): a coaching app's highest-rated property is that it refuses to let users add more habits — 'anyone shipping a habit tracker with unlimited habits is competing against the wrong thing'; the generous-cap rule is about paywalls, not about pacing. Report 25: a 3-habit free cap on a product titled 'Routines & Goals Planner' is the single largest fact in a 1,309-review corpus — 138 complaints (10.54%, mean 2.13) and 298 (22.77%) of all monetisation friction, 56% of every 1★; the cap prevents a purchase decision, not just usage ('how do you expect me to subscribe without trying anything??'), and reviewers name their own acceptable number — median 8–10; 19 defend the cap and 64 call the price fair, so the level is not the problem, the gate placement is. Cap complaints fall (17.4% → 6.7%) only because reviewers increasingly describe the whole app as locked. Report 26: a free cap of 3→5→6 habits plus a garden that stops growing at 17% — monetisation gating is 11.36% of reviews (57.8% of all 1★, 21.2% of substantive reviews) while price objection is only 0.76%; 57 defend the price and 45 call the free tier generous; the cap is the single most common reason for withholding the fifth star (47 of 535 4★: 'amazing app, but you can only add 5'); ADHD users who praise the simplicity say five slots cannot hold a morning routine. Report 27: unlimited habits on a free app is praised by name ('unlimited habit tracking without ads'; 'has no limitations'; 'i didn't need to pay to use a certain amount of habits') and 13 reviewers arrived after fleeing competitors' caps — a habit cap on the free tier 'directly attacks the stated reason users are here'. Report 28: a habit-count cap of ~8 (17, 2.07%) plus a priority-slot cap of 1 red / 2 orange (15, 1.83%) and paid moods (10); 'Had trouble finding a habit tracker that didn't need a subscription to add more than three habits' and 'free tier usage incredibly wide compared to other trackers' are stated reasons for choosing it; cap complaints fell 8.5% → 3.8% mainly because the ad load crowded them out. Report 29: 12 reviews (mean 4.92) praise the absence of a habit cap by naming competitors' caps — 'they all made me pay for more than 3 habits'; 'lets you have more than 6 habits'; 'up to 15 to 20 habits without getting charged' — the specific mechanism by which a free app wins comparison shoppers; 'do not cap habit count' is 'the single most protected property in the corpus'. Report 30: a 2-habit free cap (raised to 3 by Apr 2026) is the defining problem of a minimalist tracker — 15 reviews (9.04%, mean 2.00), 31.9% of substantive reviews, 8 of 19 one-stars and all three two-stars; 'if the app is about habits, allowing only 2 is too much'; 'it should be at least 5 free habit entry'; 'It would be smarter to create attractive features that persuade the user to pay rather than limiting tracking to a mere two'; the 2 → 3 raise changed nothing (same rate, same ratings) — an increment below the evaluability threshold does not help; the report's fix is at least 5 free and monetising depth instead of count. Report 31: a 3-habit cap (2 in 2016) drew 670 complaints (12.92%, mean 2.01) at 8–18% in every era, 13.5% in E1 and 14.0% in E4 — unchanged — while the price objection moved 4.1% → 13.0% with the subscription; the plurality objection since 2016 is evaluation ('With only 2 items makes it hard to get a feel'; 'I would like to start by tracking 5 habits, not 3'); a minority defend it ('if you've read The One Thing, three is already a lot!'); the report proposes testing 3 vs 5–6 habits vs a 14-day full trial; Spain shows the highest cap rate anywhere (28.6%). Report 33: a 3-habit cap (sometimes 2) draws 213 complaints (5.41%, mean 2.31) — 'isn't much of a test run'; 'if … 5 rather than 3 … I'd have … probably upgraded' — but is far milder than the take-backs; the report proposes testing 3 habits + unlimited check-ins vs 5 habits vs a 14-day full trial; Spain, the UK and Brazil show the highest cap rates (10.5–10.7%). Report 34: a 2-habit cap (2018–2025) is 39 complaints (5.25%, mean 2.44) and 15 of 37 1★ (40.5%), rising to 9.7% of E4; reviewers benchmark 5 as the norm ('Other apps usually have 5 free habits'; 'with three I'd have kept it for decency; with five I'd have … got hooked, and then bought'); the same cap is the most common purchase trigger for users whose two habits worked; the 2026 reports of a 4-habit tier are too few to read. Report 36: an unlimited free tier (praised: 'you can still get limitless habits w/ the free version — please keep it that way', 2023) capped at 2 then 1 in 2026; three reviewers volunteer three as the fair number ('Three would be reasonable for a paywall but only one??'; 'Ein Cap bei 3 Gewohnheiten hätte ich in Ordnung gefunden'); one mistook the cap for a bug; the cap upset US and non-US equally (5.56% each). Report 41: a 3-habit cap is 28 complaints (3.44%, mean 2.32) — 66.7% of 2★ and 31.0% of 1★, spiking to 6.4% in 2025 — while 5 describe it as a working trial and 4 of them paid; fans inside the complaint name 5–10 habits as the line ('at least 8 or 10'; '10ish'; '5/7'; '4/5'); the cap hurts 2.3× more outside high-spend markets. Report 42: a 3-habit cap where time, date, reminders and repetition are also paid is 55 complaints (26.70%, mean 1.96) — the largest theme — read as the product being broken ('Everything is paid! Writing a routine, only the title is free'; 'There is no reason to subscribe to the app to only have 3 habits'); four reviewers say the free tier proves there is no reason to subscribe; the number 3 has been cited every year 2022–2026. Report 43 (natural experiment): a 3-item cap held 2016–~2022 produced 66 complaints (10.34%, mean 2.36), 25 of 76 one-star reviews and 16 'bait and switch' accusations ('how can anyone set up a productive day with only 3 available habits?'; 'at least 8 - 10 habits for free'); loosening it removed the theme within two years and replaced it with free-tier praise at 4.63; the cap appeared at 5★ eight times from users who found three focusing; the report: do not re-tighten.

title: Daily check-in and one basic reminder per habit are free
statement: Core loop must be free; it draws no complaints when it is. Report 13: exact-clock reminder times behind the paywall was the single most resented gate in an eleven-year corpus (227 requests); free users got only Morning/Afternoon/Evening buckets. Report 25: a specific clock time per habit with a notification at that time — not a generic reminder — was absent and is the top request from satisfied users (29; 4★ band 9.0%).

title: Basic widgets, icons and colours are free
statement: Loved, drives 5★, and re-paywalling widgets backfired. Report 7: with every widget Pro, the widget paywall was the only theme with zero 5★ reviews, while widgets were the best-loved feature; users proposed one free widget, more with Pro. Report 12: widget requests appeared only from Nov 2024 and came from retained payers ('I forget all the time to use this app cause I don't have a widget') — the highest-mean complaint theme. Report 23: custom app icons and theme colours (324, 4.46%, mean 4.51) are 'a small feature with an outsized delight response'; 54 more ask for more/custom icons. Report 25: widgets (Home, Lock Screen, Control Center) are almost purely positive (30, mean 4.43, 0 1★); custom icons and colours with hex input; one lifetime buyer asks for a minimal heat-map widget like HabitKit/Ripples. Report 26: a garden-view home-screen widget, reminders, a timer and day-of-week scheduling are free (21 widget mentions, mean 4.14). Report 29: colour coding per habit is free; 4 ask for a wider palette and custom colours. Report 34: widgets requested for 3.5 years (11.1% of E3) became the top new praise on launch (11.2% of E4), then were paywalled for some users ('Cant use widgets without subscription', 1★) — the report's advice is to keep at least one widget and basic colours free. Report 36: widgets gated in Oct 2023 (WIDGETGATE 14, mean 2.64) are load-bearing for adherence — '62 days in a row … wouldn't be possible without this app and it's widgets'; 'Ojalá los widget fueran gratuitos eso mejoraría el apego' — and reviewers accept paid skins but not paid widgets ('I can understand locking skins behind a paywall but ALL widgets???'). Report 41: interactive widgets (111 mentions, 13.62%) are the most-praised surface, stronger in the US (17.4%) and GB (18.8%) than DE / CA (~9.9%). Report 42: no widgets at all, framed as a competitive deficit — 'it has no widgets, so it loses against the rest of similar apps'; 'It's a paid app, so I have higher requirements… PLEASE add a WIDGET section' (a payer). Report 43: the widget is what makes the app work for the ADHD / accessibility segment — 'if I have to seek it out a lot of the time it's not happening. I can miss notifications, but not if it's on my Home Screen' — and is named a protected surface.

title: Backfill missed days / edit start date
statement: Users accept a bounded free backfill window. Report 8 contests it: a ~7-day backfill window in a free app with weak history views was the worst-rated request (mean 3.52). Report 16: logging only today and yesterday cost earned streaks ('I forgot to log 2 days ago… my streak is permanently reset'); 33 requests from mostly 3–4★ users, unshipped for 31 months. Report 19: 'I did the habit so why can't I go back and track it?' — back-dating a completed habit was broken or absent. Report 23: 'today or yesterday?' retroactive completion and calendar backfill are included; backfill older days still requested 76 times (1.05%). Report 24: cannot undo a tick or backfill a missed day (70, mean 2.700) — the emotional cost is disproportionate because it breaks streaks the product made meaningful. Report 26: backfill the previous day and a configurable day boundary (29 verified, 0.76%) — night-owl and after-midnight complaints recur across five years; a next-day 'did you do it?' prompt exists and is praised. Report 27: backfill by tapping past dates is praised (and broke for the annual grid in 2025); two reviewers want to import an existing streak by start date ('the streak being automatically completed from that date, moving to a new phone was a bit tedious'). Report 30: editing history works inside the current month but not for prior months (asked politely by a 5★). Report 34: back-filling and long-press to mark yesterday praised by 10 (mean 4.90); editing days from the month calendar requested by 6, and one US reviewer left over it. Report 41: a payer upgraded specifically to backfill an 8-day streak and backfilling did not exist (1★); can't backfill / edit past days 5 (mean 3.40). Report 43: backfilling a day after it has passed requested by 4 (mean 3.75).

title: Weekly / monthly / yearly reports
statement: The #1 stated reason people pay; under-counted by keywords, dominant in the qualitative read. Report 25 (counter-evidence): paywalling all statistics — success %, graphs, per-habit calendar — averaged 1.40 and 'removes the motivation loop the category sells'; keep the basic progress view free, sell the deep report. Report 31: charts once unlocked are a named purchase trigger ('excited to see them … upgraded immediately'); stats 145 mentions, called weak by power users who want all-habit overviews, weekly totals and % of days. Report 33: statistics praised by 182 rated 4–5★ ('The statistics … is what sold me') and a named purchase trigger; 58 request an all-habit weekly grid, raw totals and multi-year history ('I want a GitHub type chart'); yearly and daily-ratio stats were removed in Habitify X. Report 34: statistics requests 14 (1.88%) — month %, all habits in one grid, counts rather than streaks; the free stats screen is 'a bit too simple'. Report 36: statistics / counts / year-in-review requested by 10, the newest rising request (4.6% of E5); one reviewer counts completions per month by hand. Report 41: statistics are Premium ('in free version… No statistics'), named as a purchase trigger ('love statistics now visible'), and 'better / deeper statistics' is still requested by 9. Report 42: statistics are the actual premium value proposition — three of six named purchase triggers ('Seeing the progress percentage of habits and which days they were done… because I found it in this app I bought the premium version'; 'The detailed stats in premium version are worth it') — while the same feature miscalculates for non-daily habits (a payer) and history is capped for free users. Report 43: percentages, grades, streaks and the green / red calendar praised by 55 (8.62%, mean 4.82) — 'Thank you for %'s and grades. This is how my brain works… I'm actually completing it so I can stay at a 90% grade' — free.

title: Week / month / year grid views
statement: 'Filling the squares' is the retention mechanic and emotional payoff. Report 23: statistics limited to the current and previous month (46 requests); the most-requested visualisation is a year heat-map / GitHub contribution grid, the single most-named competitor gap (Habitify). Report 25: statistics weak/unreadable (8) — rework the screen around 'why did I miss it'; a heat-map widget like HabitKit/Ripples requested. Report 26: statistics/history/calendar per habit was the top unmet need (40, 1.04% — 'this is a cosmetic habit tracker, it does not offer really understanding of progress'), something shipped ~late 2024, and the rate returned to 4.26% of substantive 2026 reviews because it is hard to find and stats cannot be reset. Report 27: daily, weekly and yearly views exist and a monthly view is the missing rung — requested five times over four years, the only feature request that repeatedly costs stars (2 of 6 3★); the year grid is the app's signature and its de-emphasis was noticed. Report 29: statistics (bar, pie, weekly analytics, completion rings) is the one advanced surface praised unprompted (10, mean 4.60) and asked to be extended — all-time records, a monthly/yearly grid, export — the safest place to add depth without violating simplicity. Report 30: per-habit and per-day completion percentages requested; history editing works only within the current month. Report 34: the per-habit year grid / 'year in pixels' / GitHub-style heatmap is the differentiator — 105 reviews (14.13%, zero 1★), 'the only habit tracker I could find with a whole year view'; 'Don't Break The Chain only makes sense if you can actually see your chain!'

title: Cloud sync / multi-device as the paid differentiator
statement: Strongest true differentiator among buyers (lift ×9.8). Report 7: absent for 3+ years, sync was the #1 3★/4★ theme with named willingness to pay; ship it opt-in and end-to-end (CloudKit private database) to keep a no-account privacy promise. Report 28: cloud sync is bundled with any purchase ('I now realize just buying anything gives u cloud access'; 'il faut payer pour jumeler les comptes'); multi-device sync is named as the advantage over Finch. Report 30: iCloud sync and colour themes are advertised paid features that no reviewer in any market or period mentions. Report 33: one purchase covering iPhone, iPad, Watch, Mac, web, Android and Windows is a leading purchase trigger — and every platform that lagged became a support case (see C251).

title: Multiple reminders per habit
statement: Moderate purchase reason; first reminder stays free. Report 25: an optional intra-day recurring reminder (every N minutes until completed) requested by 4, including a paying user's medication use case. Report 31: multiple reminders per habit were paid in the one-time era and are among what buyers value after paying. Report 33: multiple reminders per habit were moved to Premium in 2019 and cited as a paid feature buyers value ('With the premium subscription, I can add multiple reminders').

title: Shared / group habits
statement: Strong purchase driver where it exists, but the worst-executed feature — demand is proven, execution is the risk. Report 23: task sharing / accountability partner exists but is described as weak and one-way; social layer requested by 28 (0.39%). Report 24: in-app community ('Circles', 370, mean 3.897) and time-boxed group challenges exist; the word 'God' being blocked in Circles drew 14 complaints. Report 25: friends / accountability / leaderboard requested by 10 fans (mean 4.80); no social feature exists. Report 26: eight Chinese reviewers ask for the community features of the discontinued '种子习惯' (Seed Habit) app. Report 31: social / shared lists / family to-do requested by 49 (mean 3.27); a parent tracking attention to each child. Report 33: challenges, friends and sharing (2022+) are mixed (challenges 19, some gated), and the report recommends hiding them until enabled.

title: Skip / holiday / pause mode (pause a habit or counter without losing history)
statement: Minor purchase factor; free or paid open. In report 3, pause/stop/archive is the highest-leverage missing feature (44 requests at mean 4.02, 'the only thing between me and 5★'). Report 23: pausing a task and un-pausing it marked the paused days as missed and destroyed the streak — the defect defeats the feature's entire purpose; reported 2023–24 with no visible fix (57 archive/pause mentions). Report 25: vacation/pause, skip-a-day ('Jump'), mark-not-done ('Cancel') and archive all exist and are praised. Report 26: a vacation/pause mode is requested with flexible recurrence (12). Report 27: a goal end date so a completed goal stops repeating but stays visible, and habit archiving, were asked for by a 3★ reviewer — both appear on the listing and were not findable. Report 28: 'the only way to remove a habit from view is to delete it, but that results in losing all its data'; one wants to mark a routine as 'established' and retire it. Report 29: an end-date / no-end-date control requested (4) — set a habit with no end and change it later. Report 30: there is no habit end-date, so deleting a finished habit wipes its history, and Skip breaks the daily completion ring so users feel they failed a day they completed — one frequency + end-date feature closes both. Report 31: every-N-days, bi-weekly, skip, vacation mode and end dates requested by 84 (mean 3.12) — 'lose a 100+ day streak because … vacation'; a streak freeze is named as the missing piece between 4★ and 5★. Report 33: pause / vacation mode never existed (18 requests; a 'reschedule' swipe) — the report asks for a pause that preserves streaks. Report 34: skip / pause / sick day requested by 5 ('i am sick and cannot swim … i dont want to loose my results').

title: Passcode lock
statement: Minor; decide whether needed at all. Report 31: a passcode / Touch ID lock was moved behind the paywall in 2019; privacy / passcode 16 mentions. Report 33: the passcode lock was removed in 2025, a lifetime holder's complaint.

title: App-icon themes
statement: Minor purchase factor. Report 23: the alternate app icon is frequently cited as a delight (included in the one-time price). Report 33: per-habit colours and themes requested by 48 ('I dislike blue … would pay more').

title: Quit-habit / bad-habit mode
statement: Well received where shipped; see Quit Habit Decision research doc. Report 23: negative ('don't') tasks shipped in v3.0, Jul 2017. Report 25: a 'bad habit' mode exists and counts against the cap; a bad-habit limit exceeded at 200% is scored as success; a long review asks whether to name it 'smoked' or 'didn't smoke'. Report 31: build and quit habits in one list is praised by 96 ('the ONLY app I've found that does that'); quit-to-zero goals were removed in Mar 2022 and Jan 2023 (sobriety tracking), and 30 find quit/zero-goal habits confusing — restore them. Report 33: bad-habit / limit tracking done well requested by 23 — a tap per cigarette, auto-fail over the limit. Report 34: bad-habit / quit tracking 6 — 'I'd rather not see TO DO next to bad habits'. Report 36: a quit-a-habit inverse mode requested once. Report 41: break-a-bad-habit mode (max units per day) praised by 36 (mean 4.69); Screen Time as a trackable bad habit requested by 4. Report 43: negative / 'avoid' habit tracking requested by 3.

title: Data export / backup / CSV
statement: Requested a lot from happy users, rarely a purchase trigger — charging for it generates requests, not revenue. Report 18: export was asked for from the app's fifth month to its last, named as a purchase condition twice ('add export and I'll subscribe for life'), and is the honest answer to five years of unresolved data-loss reports — it lets users protect themselves. Report 20: export never shipped (9 requests, mean 4.44). Report 23: CSV export is included in the one-time price. Report 25: CSV export exists but is described as weak (3). Report 27: data export is praised ('export data for nerdy kind') and the one-tap note export was removed in 2025, producing the only 2★. Report 28: no export mentioned; cloud sync paid. Report 29: add a local CSV/JSON export to Files, account-free, so a date bug can never again mean total loss — three independent export/backup requests. Report 31: backup to Dropbox/iCloud and CSV export were manual only with a repeated backup nag; export hangs ('I can't export my data to move to another app because it hangs on the CSV export') — export is the exit door, keep it open and fast; export to Google Drive was a purchase trigger. Report 33: CSV export was removed with Habitify X (Aug 2020) and back from 2022. Report 34: CSV export disabled in Feb 2026 ('Out of nowhere … years of data are stuck in this app'; 'Vendor Lock', 1★) and a paid backup required before deleting (1★) — both data-lock-in reviews are 1★ (mean 1.00) in a no-account app where export is the only exit. Report 41: CSV export shipped Feb 2023 after a year of requests ('Now that the developer has added CSV export… the app is 5-star awesome for me') and is named as a purchase reason ('so my data is safe'); praised by 14 (mean 4.71). Report 42: no export or backup; history beyond ~2 weeks paywalled ('if you don't pay you won't see last month's result'). Report 43: CSV / PDF export requested by 2; no export exists in a local-storage app that lost four-year histories.

title: Apple Health integration
statement: Small volume, very high purchase intent. Report 23: HealthKit auto-completion (277, 3.81%, mean 4.35) is 'the single highest-leverage integration in the category' — it removes the friction that killed every other habit app the reviewer tried; a weak tail of misfires (auto-completing without action 11; Health data miscounting 9). Report 25: two-way Apple Health is a purchase trigger (32, 2.44%) with a weak tail of demonstrably wrong mappings — weight read as an entry count, steps off by 568, running only measurable in minutes, step counting starting at 04:00 (9, 0.69%). Report 27: Apple Health integration (exercise, water, steps, sleep) requested once, 4★. Report 31: Apple Health integration covers ~10 preset tasks (steps, sleep, exercise minutes); 79 mentions (mean 2.85); Health sync named as the missing piece between 4★ and 5★. Report 33: Apple Health auto-logging and Fitbit, Strava, screen-time and NFC habits, described as both free and Premium; Health integration complaints rose to 2.2% of E5 and Garmin / wearable auto-completion is requested. Report 36: Apple Health requested by 3 — a 10,000-step habit that auto-completes. Report 41: Apple Health auto-completion (53 mentions) is a switch reason ('Coming from Grit, I almost instantly bought it because the Apple Health habits actually work') and a payer failure ('I paid for it specifically for synching with the health app'); Health gaps 8. Report 43: Apple Health integration requested once.

title: Apple Watch app (done properly: timer, two-way sync)
statement: Small volume, very high purchase intent; a half-built Watch app draws 2–3★. Report 20: an Apple Watch app was the highest-mean capability gap (62 requests, mean 4.15), asked for by the happiest users and named in churn-to-Streaks reviews; never shipped. Report 23: the Watch is the app's strongest differentiator and most fragile surface — 626 mentions (8.61%), 241 negative (mean 3.13) vs 385 positive (mean 4.35); it breaks on each watchOS generation (2016, watchOS 7, 2021–22 mirroring, watchOS 10 complications, 2024–26 blank complications); in Korea (13.5%) and Japan (13.3%) it is the dominant topic; 'I bought this for the Watch and it doesn't work' are the highest-value churn events. Report 24: in a 43,469-review coaching corpus the Watch (69, 0.16%) and widget (53, 0.12%) are marginal — the surface matters where the product is a checklist, not where it is content. Report 25: the Watch app (21 mentions, mean 4.48, 0 1★) is part of a praised Apple-platform surface (Watch + Mac + widgets + Shortcuts + Health), but one reviewer says it was 'suddenly removed' (Oct 2025) and another that the listing advertised Watch support that could not be installed. Report 26: no Apple Watch app throughout; requested by 8 (0.21%). Report 27: Apple Watch, Apple Health and macOS are each requested once (4★ 'Would be perfect with watch support'); the report says a paid tier, if ever, should attach only to such not-yet-existing capability. Report 31: the Watch app and complication were broken for long periods — 60 reviews (mean 2.33); support asked for a video, then silence; ''update coming soon'. 6 months later'; the v2 rebuild (Mar 2022) broke it and restored it months later. Report 33: the Watch app broke with iOS 13, would not launch after Habitify X, its complication broke with iOS 15.1 and sync lagged until 'finally' fixed Jan 2024 — 100 reviews (2.84 mean), 6.8% of E3, Japan 5.0% ('Streaks costs a tenth and works'); single-tap logging and area complications were removed. Report 36: Apple Watch requested by 9 (mean 4.11), one wanting the haptics on the wrist. Report 41: the Watch app shipped in 2021 on request (discussion peaked 13.7% then normalised); a privacy-minded payer cancelled because Watch sync requires iCloud and will return for 'easy normal Bluetooth sync between the phone and the watch'. Report 43: Apple Watch requested by 12 over five years (May 2019 'Not using your app due to lack of iwatch' → Jan 2024), the listing now ships Watch, and no request appears after Jan 2024.

title: Interactive widget check-off
statement: Mark done without opening the app; small volume, very high intent. Report 18: 'let me check off without launching the app' was the single most-repeated widget request across five years and every language; some builds fixed it (Jul 2025) and then it regressed. Report 23: an interactive Today-view widget shipped Jan 2017 to enthusiasm, was lost at iOS 14 (Sept 2020) and asked for back continuously for five years (36 named requests) — one of the top three reasons for a downgrade from a previously-happy user; restore it via App Intents. Report 26: an interactive widget to tick from the home screen requested (~5); the garden-view widget is free. Report 27: reviewers wrote the widget spec — 'a small widget that just showed the current streak count for a single goal'; 'a streak counter on the widget like duolingo'; 'a grayed out version if it's still to do and a coloured version if it's done'; tappable to check off — requested in 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026; in a streak app the widget is the retention surface. Report 28: an interactive check-off widget requested continuously for four and a half years by satisfied users (mean 4.64, zero negatives). Report 29: a Home Screen widget showing today's list requested by 16 across 26 months, 7 of them in 2026. Report 31: a tappable Today-view widget (2018–2021) was replaced in Oct 2021 by a non-interactive home/lock-screen widget limited to 4 habits (a user with a memory disability 'requesting a refund'); before that, the app had no iOS 14 widget for a year — 73 of 451 reviews (16.2%) Sep 2020 – Sep 2021 and 14.0% of E2 asked about it; the widget peaks in the 4★ band (12.6% vs 3.8%). Report 33: the 2016 Today widget was removed ('the entire reason I paid'), iOS 14 widgets were non-interactive, and the May 2025 redesign removed compact, incremental (+1) and streak widgets — widget complaints 6.3% of 2025, the one surface still worsening; interactive widgets named as the 4★ → 5★ piece. Report 34: 7 interactive-widget requests, all after static widgets shipped (Mar 2024) — 'The widgets still aren't interactive' (Feb 2026). Report 36: 'instead of taking advantage of the iOS 17 update with interactive widgets, they preferred to make that option paid' (2★); interactive widget requested by 4.

title: Streaks / gamification
statement: High-priority praise, moderate purchase factor. Report 10 (contested): streaks added to a non-punitive pet app generated their own defect stream (171, growing 74×) and pressure stream (96) — net-negative in the written record for an ADHD audience. Report 20: a streak counter was requested 71 times (mean 3.72) — always alongside, never instead of, the decaying strength score. Report 23: streak psychology is the highest-satisfaction theme (902, 12.41%, mean 4.75, 0.7% 1★ — reviewers get out of bed to preserve a streak); rewards/badges/levels are requested by fans (136, 1.87%, mean 4.43). Report 24: streak counters with 'freeze' passes and certificates; Duolingo is named for its streak freezes. Report 27: streaks are the core praised mechanic in a deliberately non-gamified app — no pets, no flashy graphics, no urgency; behaviour-change outcomes ('I'm on a 9 day vacuuming streak!') rose 0% → 11.9% across eras. Report 28: gamification (carrots, levels, rooms, a pet) is the differentiator in an 821-review corpus — but 10 (mean 2.40) say 'it's a game, not a tracker', an expectation mismatch the listing could pre-empt. Report 31: motivation through bars filling, streaks and sounds is praised by 200 rated 4–5★ ('an adult sticker chart!'); removing the streak count from the main list in v3.0 drew 52 complaints (100% E4), including medication and 30-day pill-cycle users; the report proposes a streak-on-list toggle and testing its default on logging frequency. Report 33: motivation / streaks praised by 130 (mean 4.75); non-daily streaks broke and the streak count on the complete button changed in redesigns.

title: Scholarship / hardship / discount program
statement: The cleanest 5★ generator in report 1 (91 of 101 mentions 5★); also works around broken payment rails; never switch it off. Report 10: a 'Guardian' pay-it-forward sponsorship programme is one of the only monetisation themes with a positive mean (4.76 across 708 mentions); its one complaint is that there is no visible way to apply. Report 31: ~110 teen and low-income reviewers (2.12%, mean 2.31) in the 2022–23 TikTok cohort ('your target market at this point is us teenagers'; ages 14, 12, 11; a mental-health user who can't work) — lead with a student / low-income price in those markets. Report 34: a 50% annual offer converted ('I paid £9.99 for a whole year - bargain!'), affordability complaints come from students, Vietnam and ADHD users; the report proposes a student / regional price and New-Year sales. Report 36: AFFORD 5 (mean 2.20) — two on disability, a student, and 'there is no way I can afford it without being part of the demographic which can drop 60$ on a reminder app'. Report 41: a high-school student asks for a student deal; a Turkish 5★ says the one-time fee is too much 'at least in my country'; the report proposes purchasing-power-adjusted lifetime tiers in the long-tail storefronts. Report 42: 'I was ready to pay, but it has to be reasonable… I'm sure if you lower the price, revenue will grow' (RU); price objections at $39.99–$59.99 in high-income markets vs '500₽ a year, that's nothing'.

title: Handle markets where card payment fails (RU, AR, TR, DZ, PK)
statement: Users who want to pay cannot; a discount/hardship path doubles as the workaround. Report 26: 16 reviews (mean 4.06 — willing buyers, not complaints) cannot pay — 8 Russian ('the trial button is not clickable… possibly because I live in Russia'; cards cannot be linked), 3 Chinese/Taiwanese ('tap subscribe and nothing happens'; a ¥38 tier shown with no in-app path), 2 Vietnamese (ShopeePay / MoMo requested); Russia is 19.18% of the corpus and its highest-satisfaction market — the highest-yield-per-effort monetisation item. Report 42: 'there's no way to pay from Russia' (Jun 2026) — a market with the worst defect exposure receiving paywall pressure it cannot convert.

title: Localise early — it unlocks revenue
statement: Missing localisation is the biggest market-specific complaint and a stated purchase blocker; shipping a language visibly converts (Japan). Report 10: localisation is HIGH-PRIORITY at country level in eight storefronts at once (cn 26%, ru 18%, tr 19%, br 13%, es 12%); reviewers say they will not pay in English. Report 13: Arabic is the largest unserved language (20.5% of Saudi reviews); users were also served the wrong language ('I am from Turkey but this app language is Korean', 41 votes) and shown store screenshots in languages the app does not have. Report 18: Japanese Instagram ads led to an app that opened in Korean with a KakaoTalk login; Korean push notifications persisted a year after the UI was fixed, the terms page stayed English-only (one reviewer refused to trial for that reason), Traditional Chinese was largely Simplified wording, and a Dutch translation was unintelligible. Report 19: an Instagram ad ran in Spanish for an English-only app — 'tell me if there's a Spanish version and if not, refund the money'. Report 20: Russian-first UI leaked to Chinese, French and Swiss users, Chinese localisation existed and was later removed ('there was Chinese a few years ago'), and Ukrainian was requested and never added. Report 23: bad German localisation ('Die Übersetzung ins Deutsche ist total fehlgeschlagen') undercut the premium price in the corpus's worst large market (mean 3.62); machine-translated Chinese help text drew 52 upvotes and was still cited seven years later; localisation-quality complaints span de, ru, se, kr, cn, tw, jp and es (mixed EN/ES notifications, English-only icon search); a Hangul IME bug went unfixed five years. Report 24: the praise vocabulary (small steps, coaching, art, 'life-changing') appears in every language and the forced-water complaint in six; language requests concentrate in Vietnam, Uzbekistan, Russia, Brazil and Italy; Germany praises the app's craft at 19.61% (3× the corpus); China (1,250 reviews, mean 3.431, 28.6% 1★) is unreadable by an English-anchored classifier. Report 25: localisation demand is new and growing (0% → 1.0% → 2.7%; Turkish 9, Korean 3, Italian 3, Russian/Ukrainian 3, Chinese 2, Japanese 1); Korea and China are 100% 5★ and 75%/50% localisation requests ('If there is Chinese, it will definitely be loved by the Chinese market') — reached only by users tolerant of an English UI; Turkish shipped Jul 2026 and the review stream responded. Report 26: localisation requests in Arabic, Thai and Spanish; Russian localisation quality criticised in 2023 ('hire a competent localiser') and praised by 2025; the German store listing carried a typo ('Gewohnheitstrinker' — habit drinker); Chinese reviewers ask for the community features of a discontinued app ('种子习惯'); the cn aesthetic rate of 3.12% is a classifier artefact. Report 27: localisation is not an issue — zero complaints across seven non-English reviews; the two Monday-week-start requests (DE, AU) are the only regional-convention issue. Report 28: 21 localisation requests/defects (2.56%) — Spanish 5, Turkish 3, Chinese 3, Japanese 2, Russian 2, French, Thai, Arabic, Portuguese; two are defects on an existing localisation (Japanese glyphs rendered for Chinese, habit names truncated; untranslated English with Chinese selected) and a 2022 localisation update rendered every 'r' as a black square; rest-of-world markets rate higher (4.181 vs 3.956) and are 5× more blocked by language (5.56% vs 1.09%) — 'the cheapest lever in the highest-satisfaction segment'; two name language as why they leave. Report 29: the listing supports 8 languages and not Spanish or Russian, yet 8 Spanish-language reviews arrive from UZ/CL/MX/AR/ES/US and one is blocked ('No puedo cambiar la lengua, ayuden me por favor') — Spanish first is the cheapest defensible localisation case. Report 30: 13 languages functioning and one explicit localisation compliment from Chile; an Arabic onboarding blocker; 11 reviews in a language not matching their storefront. Report 31: 61 localisation requests (1.18%) and French and German reviewers say localisation is their purchase condition ('J'achèterai la version premium quand elle sera traduite en français'; didn't buy Pro because there was no German); China is the happiest storefront (4.09) and the loudest localisation demand (23.9% — '无中文无满分', no Chinese, no full marks); Ukraine 26.7%, Russia 13.6%, France 11.3%; recommended: Spanish, Portuguese, Chinese, German, French, Russian. Report 33: localisation grievances are about quality — 「たどたどしい日本語」 (halting Japanese), simplified-Chinese glyphs in Japanese, an offensive German UI string ('Pisst du dabei?'), a lost Russian UI, English-only support replies — 62 reviews (1.57%); Chinese reviewers praise the localisation; Arabic users ask for an Arabic UI; motivational copy read as 'far too American and over the top' in the Netherlands. Report 34: 19 polite localisation requests (none 1★) — Chinese 9, Russian 4, Spanish 2, French 2, Ukrainian 1 — 11 of them arriving in E3, starting the day a free-lifetime promotion reached br, vn, cn and co: promote into a market only once the app speaks its language. Report 36: localisation requests were 7.0% of E1 (six Chinese-market, May–June 2022, plus MX 1★ 'solo esté en inglés me hace perder el interés') and stopped after mid-2022, consistent with localisation shipping. Report 41: shipping Italian and Traditional Chinese (Jun 2026) brought reviewers straight back to rate 5★ ('I ran straight here to give 5 stars'); missing Spanish blocked a purchase ('es por eso que aún no acabo de lanzarme a comprarla'); Russian — requested from five unrelated storefronts — is the largest unserved language; non-English storefronts like the app equally (4.581) but self-report paying at 5.52% vs 9.9%. Report 42: Russian-language support was the original wedge in Russia ('the competitor has no Russian'), and Russia is both the most appreciative and the most defect-exposed market — where users now cannot pay at all. Report 43: all 10 language requests are non-US (4.37% of non-US reviews) — Arabic three times in fourteen months from Saudi Arabia and Oman, each capping the rating at exactly 3★ ('Nice app but it lacks Arabic support, so it deserves ⭐️⭐️⭐️'); Portuguese and Spanish requests appear answered by the listing's five languages; one 'full of spelling mistakes' (GB, 1★).

title: Culturally complete icon set and calendars
statement: Islamic icons, disability icons, Hijri and lunar calendars, bigger fonts — cheap, and in markets already blocked by localisation.

title: Billing must be exactly right
statement: Wrong amount, double charge, surprise renewal are the fastest route to 1★ (×21 lift); single price shown, no trial-to-charge traps, refunds honoured, receipts clear. Report 19: a 105-review corpus that was 91% one-star and 71% about money — charged after cancelling (19), charged with no recognised subscription (19), double-billed (16), charged ≠ agreed ($29.99 annual agreed, $59.99/month billed), and terms permitting weekly renewal made 'again and again every week' structurally possible. Report 23: nothing supports deceptive billing on a single Apple payment; refund friction (79, mean 1.75, 70.9% 1★) is Apple's process, and reviewers address Apple through the review field. Report 24: charged after cancelling 1,620 (3.73%, mean 1.085), duplicate charges 584, charge without consent 338 (mean 1.047), not visible in Apple Subscriptions 125 — all consequences of billing outside Apple IAP; 1,412 edited reviews are mostly downgrades after a later charge. Report 31: billing-dispute language in 403 reviews (7.77%, mean 1.24) — refund, scam, fraud, estafa, arnaque, Abzocke, 欺诈 in eight languages — with 13 calling on Apple to remove the developer; billing & entitlement integrity rose 1.6% (E1) → 34.5% (E4) → 25.4% (E5): 768 reviews (14.81%, mean 1.30); discount offers checked out at full price in 69 (49 actually charged; '$59.99 crossed out and … $9.99 … My card was charged full price'; support: 'a bug that happens sometimes') — make the displayed price the charged price and audit introductory-offer configuration per storefront (CA, AU, GB, DE first). Report 33: billing integrity 147 (3.73%, mean 2.22) — charged more than shown (¥4,900 shown, ¥5,150 charged; a $39.99 offer charged $48.97; monthly chosen, annual charged; lifetime then an annual charge); billing-dispute register 「詐欺アプリ」, 'Abzocke', 'CON ARTISTS', 流氓. Report 36: all 3 billing reviews are 1★ — a cancellation link that returns 'Cannot cancel subscription' ('roach motel'), an unauthorised annual charge on a disabled reviewer, and five annual fees for one bundle membership with two refunds denied (China) — triaged regardless of 0.56% share as the only consumer-protection records. Report 42: three payers charged without intending — 'immediately charged for a subscription upon opening the app for the first time'; 'auto-selected a package and deducted money… hadn't even tried it' (499k₫); a promotional R$39.90/year that became R$99.90 at checkout — plus a trial that 'won't get the refund even if you cancel two minutes after'; 11 of 29 writing payers (37.9%) request refunds.

title: Sync must work — and prove it
statement: The paid feature that breaks most; sync failure is ×12.8 over-represented among buyers. Report 13: iCloud sync complaints rose 10× from 2015 to 2021 and ran at 8.9% of 3★ reviews — the fastest-worsening dimension and the defect most likely costing renewals. Report 23: sync is the single largest reliability finding — 348 mentions (4.79%), 223 complaint-framed (3.07%, mean 3.08, 23.3% 1★), only 22 positive; the 2022 migration produced a spike (25 → 60 → 40 → 24 by year) with visible recoveries within weeks and a tail still visible in 2026 — a migration with a long, damaging tail; Germany 10.0%, Spain 10.1%, Sweden 9.7%. Report 25: cross-device sync not updating 14 (1.07%, mean 3.29), flat across eras. Report 27: sync that works but cannot be seen produces data-loss anxiety (4) and sync requests (3 — iPad; 'wish my goals were synced across my devices') in a corpus where the listing says iCloud sync already exists. Report 31: sync / backup / restore fails in 83 reviews ('Manual syncing is so 2010'); real-time iCloud sync across iPhone, iPad and Watch is requested with the iPad layout, concentrated in the 4★ band. Report 33: account-only (Firebase) sync replaced personal iCloud sync ('Original Habitify was able to sync … over personal iCloud. This has been removed'), with repeated logouts; sync failures 119 (3.02%), 7.9% of E4 — offer iCloud sync as an option alongside the account backend. Report 36: private sync is the resolution of the privacy-vs-sync tension — local-only praised ('not harvesting your data') while sync is the top request. Report 41: cross-device iCloud sync with no account is praised by 90 (11.04%) and fails for 13 (1.60%, mean 3.08) — four of them payers, because sync is the promise the app is bought on. Report 43: iCloud is simultaneously the advertised backup, an undismissable error banner ('iCloud Sign in Error - I can't turn off this message'; 'Constant iCloud Error… Sloppy code') and a backup that did not restore for a payer ('lost everything even though it was backed up to iCloud') — 5 reviews, mean 1.40, none after Aug 2022.

title: Crashes / launch failures
statement: Largest complaint by volume; a two-day launch crash produced more 1★ than years of minor bugs. Report 23: crashes 46 (0.63%, mean 2.80, 34.8% 1★) on three dated bugs — iPhone X freeze-on-close 2017–18, an iOS 14-era freeze, a stuck splash screen 2023–26 — plus Watch-app crashes on each watchOS generation. Report 24: crash / freeze / won't load 944 (2.17%, mean 2.367) — the recurring shape is freezing on the 'first mountain' / Journeys screen on day one. Report 25: a post-onboarding freeze — the main screen stops responding to touch — is the fastest-rising negative theme (51, 3.90%, mean 1.63; 1.3% → 2.9% → 5.8%; 27 of 34 E3 reports in May–Jul 2026; Colombia 18%, Germany 7.8%, GB 0%); iPhone 11 and iOS 26.x named, reinstalling does not fix it, one reviewer says it survived two updates; every one of these users got zero value. Report 26: crash/launch failure fell 3.37% (2021–22) → 0.13% (2024) after a visible engineering turnaround, then a 2026 cluster (n=4, three Russian, two paying — a premium subscriber crashing on the onboarding screen after reinstall) flagged for telemetry. Report 27: a September–November 2025 update-and-iOS-26 launch crash ('Ever since I updated to iOS 26 the app immediately crashes when I try to open') accounts for almost every bad rating the app ever received — all 4 1★, the only 2★ and 4 of 6 3★ fall in a five-week window (window mean 4.162 vs 4.822 elsewhere); fixed by Feb 2026 (mean 4.829, zero 1★); a solo-developer app with no support channel pays for an OS-transition break entirely in public rating. Report 28: launch failure / crash 15 (1.83%, mean 2.40) concentrated in 2022 (orange-screen failure), then a 2026 uptick ('freezing every time I open the app, I think it needs an update to keep up with ios') consistent with OS drift on a build last updated Nov 2025. Report 29: one 2026 launch failure ('Lässt sich nichtmal öffnen'); overall bug reporting fell by two-thirds (22.3% → 6.5%). Report 30: two launch-week crashes (Jul 2025, 'It just doesn't open… on iOS 18.5 and on the iOS 26 beta') and none in the following 13 months. Report 31: the app would not open in 1,052 reviews (20.29%, mean 1.30) in five waves — launch season 2016, intro freeze Oct–Dec 2021, v1.19.0 crash on launch 22 Dec 2021 → ~8 Jan 2022 (918 in the window), a post-update white-screen hang May–Jun 2022, freezes after subscribing 2022–23; devices from iPhone 6 to 12 Pro Max, so not an old-device issue; 1★ in E3 is 66.4% launch failures; the fix did not recur at scale. Report 33: an 11 Sep 2025 'Liquid glass' update crashed on launch on iOS 18 and was fixed in ~1–3 days with no lasting rating shift; in Oct–Nov 2019 Brazilian users could not open the app after purchase. Report 34: the 10–11 Apr 2024 update crashed on launch and was fixed a day later (E4 reliability 6.7% → E5 2.6%); in Feb 2026 a reviewer needed 20–30 launches to load. Report 42: a launch-blocking regression 4 Dec 2024 – 11 Jan 2025 — 7 'won't open' reviews (mean 1.71), 5 Russian inside 40 days, one a payer three months into an annual subscription ('Give my money back, crooks'). Report 43: crash / won't open is the largest single defect (20, 3.13%, mean 2.15; 18 of 20 US) with a persistent won't-open cluster Dec 2021 → Feb 2023 recurring Dec 2025 → Apr 2026; 'after purchasing, the app crashed every single time I opened it'; 'Crashes if you have less than 500MB free'.

title: New Year peak-season robustness — year-end report and January onboarding
statement: The year-end report crashed five New Years in six; never ship risk or lock features in late December. The New Year cohort is the largest of the year and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day defect is amplified ~2× in January (reports 8, 9). The New Year cohort is the largest of the year and judges onboarding, not retention — every create-flow or first-day defect is amplified ~2× in January (reports 8, 9). Report 31: v1.19.0 shipped a crash on launch on 22 Dec 2021, into the New Year and a TikTok-driven install surge — 1,135 reviews in 25 days (21.89% of the corpus, 79.4% 1★, 51% non-US), 35% of lifetime 1★; 47 reviewers never got to use the app; collateral data loss ('Lost more than 2 years of data'); the 2022 mean of 1.74 is a release-engineering outcome — stage rollouts and freeze releases before acquisition or seasonal peaks.

title: Restore purchase and entitlements must work immediately
statement: Charging and not delivering is the second-fastest route to 1★ (×13.9). Lifetime buyers told to subscribe, subscribers who cannot find their tier, premium members still upsold. Report 11: 3 of 3 paid reviewers lost purchased access — a lifetime non-consumable expired, a subscription re-locked after a week and reinstall did not restore, an active annual term was re-charged — and two titled their reviews 'scam' and 'Purchase fraud'. Report 12: 40% of self-identified payers reported that payment did not grant access (paywall re-appears, 'no subscription found', Restore Purchase redirecting to the privacy policy, HTTP 400 at login, re-purchase demanded on a new device) — rising to 12.6% of all 2025 reviews. Report 18: 25 entitlement failures (mean 2.44★; 9.94% of confirmed payers; every Japanese instance 1★) — lifetime buyers denied Pro, a PayPay lifetime never applied, a subscription active in iOS settings with premium unusable, and a lifetime holder whose entitlement was deleted when they cancelled an accidental annual plan. The worst case: a power cut reset a lifetime buyer to onboarding, wiped every routine, then demanded a subscription. Report 19: 5 of 105 paid and could not use the product — 'I can log in on my laptop but no apps'; iPhone login error 300 with no message while iPad worked; account access lost once cancellation was started. Report 20: legacy lifetime entitlements often did not survive a device change; restore-purchase failures (91, mean 1.59) recurred for years after the 2021 revocation, and 75.8% of them came from confirmed payers. Report 25: 'already paid, asked to pay again' — 8 reviews across a 16-month window (Mar 2025 → Jul 2026), including a lifetime purchase that restore does not recognise ('every time I enter the app it tells me to remove them or to buy the subscription to keep my habits'); emerging by rate, severe by kind, and the persistence argues against a one-off outage. Report 26: purchase lost or not delivered is the top paid-user failure (24, 0.63%; 12 of 72 explicit payers = 16.7%) by three mechanisms — the 2022 repricing withdrew a purchased unlock, restore-purchases fails or the button is dead, payment succeeded but premium never activated. Report 28: 10 of 24 identifiable payers (41.7%) report a purchase not delivered or not restorable — a $9.99 pack that never appeared with 'no Support button in the app. Nor on developer's website'; restore failing on a new device with the same account; a purchased cosmetic that reverted; consumables cannot be restored the way non-consumables can. Report 30: 'Списаны деньги за подписку, премиум функция не открылась' — charged with premium never unlocked — 'unambiguously a bug and should be treated as a P0 incident, not a review'; both billing failures are Russian, the only market with continuous purchase attempts. Report 31: 468 reviews (9.02%, mean 1.23; 304 explicit payers) say Premium they paid for was not granted — 2023 200, 2024 200 — including 295 'lifetime' buyers who stayed on Basic (mean 1.14, 89.5% 1★): the post-purchase 'gift' / Growth-Bundle screen appears to drop the entitlement when dismissed ('by not finishing this flow and purchasing the upsell, I think it doesn't recognize I purchased it'); one clean success ('I was successful at purchasing and using a lifetime premium upgrade') suggests a code-path defect that ran at least 16 months — make the entitlement grant atomic with the purchase and show any cross-sell after. Report 33: entitlement failure is small (69, 1.75%) and mostly portability — web (Paddle) purchases not unlocking the iPhone, a lifetime tied to one e-mail and paid twice, guest → account, a new or stolen phone, 18 days without activation, 6+ weeks and 20+ e-mails to resolve, a lifetime holder asked to subscribe on the Watch — plus a Jan 2018 wave (21, 11 in Japan) fixed within two weeks; the report asks for one entitlement per person recognised on every platform, with guest and account purchases merged automatically. Report 36: entitlements don't travel — skins 'unlocking them on each device'; a payer who cannot find out whether the subscription covers one device. Report 41: premium bought on iPhone never reached the iPad (2022) and premium intermittently reverted to free with Restore Purchases failing (2025) — 'a paying customer being shown a paywall is the most damaging possible bug'.

title: Data must never be lost on update, reinstall or phone change
statement: Data loss is ×10.6 over-represented among buyers; local-only storage is the cause. Report 10: from 2025 the dominant story became app-initiated — 'it told me my pet data got corrupted' — with no automatic backup to fall back on. Report 14: data lost on update was the only theme with a perfect 1★ record and the corpus's only 'stay away' review; it recurred 5.5 years later ('backdate all my progress by memory (again)'). Report 18: data loss sat between 6% and 8% in every era after the first, five years running — the single most durable defect in a 2,048-review corpus — and hit 12.42% of confirmed payers; 'if I'd known records could all disappear I wouldn't have paid.' Report 20: update 1.41.0 (13 Mar 2025) erased habit histories globally — 126 of 161 reviews in the following seven weeks (78.3%) reported losing 2–5 years; the advertised fix did not work, a second bug wiped prior progress on the next check-off, iCloud backup was itself a paid, manual feature ('Why should a premium subscriber even have to think about whether a backup was created?'), and there was no communication. The same migration-bug class had fired in Jan 2021. Report 23: data loss 81 (1.11%, mean 2.17, 45.7% 1★), 60 of them after the 2022 sync rewrite (3.38% of post-2022 reviews, mean 2.03; 2024 peak 22) — the only theme that destroys a long-tenure customer outright ('my 3+ years record to null'; 'It's like I'm a brand new user'); an in-app backup existed and was discovered by support, not the user. Report 24: progress lost on device change with no restore (257, mean 2.693) is the most-cited reason a multi-year user stops. Report 25: data loss / reset to zero 12 (0.92%), flat ~1%; archive/delete destroys history (4) — 'archive losing history defeats the point of archiving'. Report 26: with no account or sync, a support-recommended reinstall deleted 'all the lovely growth you have achieved' along with the purchase. Report 27: the one observed churn — 'It doesnt open with the update, ive lost all my progress, guess its time for a new app' — is reliability plus data loss, not price. Report 28: 12 data/progress-loss reports (1.46%, mean 2.42) entangled with the game's intentional decay — 'on challenge mode… run out of health it resets ALL of your progress… level 278… resets you to level 1'; 'My Account is gone, I was at a high Level'; an intentional decay mechanic and an unintentional data-loss bug are indistinguishable to the user. Report 29: 9 data-loss reports (mean 2.11, the lowest-rated theme) came from the calendar bug plus a workaround users taught each other — reinstall — which wiped local-only history ('just sad I lost my data from uninstalling it'); 'the bug fix alone does not close this loop — an export or backup path does'. Report 31: data / streaks lost or reset in 94 reviews (a 109-day no-wine streak; sobriety 40 → 16 days; 200+ day streaks to 0); counts corrupted by v2.7.1/2.7.2 in 107 (58,720 — 'Do not download 2.7.2!!!'); a habit tracker's only durable asset is the user's history, which users treat as health data — gate releases on data-migration tests and stage every rollout. Report 33: v2.0 (Nov 2016) wiped history and Premium for many ('30 routines gone'); Habitify X erased 4 months of time logs; data lost 55 reviews (mean 2.25). Report 34: local-only storage lost data on reinstall, factory reset or 'for no reason' (4; 'thought this app supports iCloud sync and re-installed app … lost all data as this app needs backup file'). Report 36: 'everything you save and track is reset when the app is deleted … I do not recommend' (1★); DATALOSS 3 (mean 1.67); a new phone met the new cap ('5 habits on the old phone, 1 on the new'). Report 41: 6 data-loss reports (0.74%, mean 3.33) — 'After 215 days of tracking… everything… deleted, all history lost! No chance to restore'; 'deleted from BOTH old and new device' on migration; one recovered only by the developer by hand; a 6-month total loss filed at 5★. Report 42: data loss 6 (mean 1.33, acted on regardless of share) — 'last night it updated… All my data and tracking… is gone'; 'I had 90 days of progress on every habit, now it's all gone and became 9 days'; 'I used it for many years… After the last update progress isn't visible… looking for a replacement' — the update → restart → history-truncated pattern recurs, four of six Russian. Report 43: data loss is the most severe and accelerating defect — 12 (1.88%, mean 2.08), 0 in 2016–18 → 7 in 2022–26 (4.55%); in July 2026 two German users four days apart lost four years of locally stored history when the UI changed ('I used HabitHub for four years and after an update my locally stored data was gone'), got immediate support replies, and had already migrated — 'If I could change anything, I would sync my data to the iCloud to be sure'.

title: Account system from day one
statement: Root cause of lost purchases, lost data and failed sync; requests rise as users change phones. Report 20: 'no account, no signup' was praised — and was the root cause of the 2025 data loss; the account/backup layer must exist even if signup stays optional. Report 26: no account system anywhere in the corpus — a device change, a reinstall, or support's own advice to reinstall destroys both progress and entitlement ('It also deletes the purchase price of the app if you bought it as there is no account to sign into'); absent accounts every other entitlement bug is unrecoverable — the root cause behind the top paid-user complaint. Report 27 (counter-evidence on the signup side, not the durability side): no account is praised — but iCloud sync exists and is invisible, so three reviewers fear data loss and one churned after an update lost progress; the account layer's job here is legible backup, not signup. Report 28: an account with e-mail verification exists (29 mentions, mean 3.66, mixed); a verification reset by support turned a 1★ into a 5★. Report 29 (counter-evidence): no account, no email, no login is named as the reason to choose the app; the report's rule is backup yes, account no — local-first. Report 33: guest mode is a data trap — 26 users who never created an account lost everything on update, reinstall or Mac sign-in ('Never use guest mode'; a ¥6,000 lifetime bought as a guest) — while forced login since 2016 is itself a privacy complaint. Report 36: no account at all; Chinese-market users ask for login specifically ('希望可以登陆', 17 helpful votes, third most-voted). Report 41 (counter-evidence): no account is praised (privacy / no account 10, all 5★: 'Pas de compte à créer, pas de données collectées'), and the report lists 'do not require an account' among what not to change. Report 43 (counter-evidence): no account required is listed among reasons to buy ('No subscription · Very reasonable one-time purchase price · Great data privacy (no data collected) · No ads').

title: A support channel that exists, is reachable outside the app, and answers
statement: 'No support channel' is ×34.7 over-represented among buyers and the second-worst-rated complaint. Report 5: the only support link was inside an app that would not launch; email went unanswered while public review replies were same-day. Report 10: AI and canned support replies; paying users 13× over-represented among support complaints. Report 11: 'there is no way in app to talk with developer or team' — with no support queue, billing bugs were filed as public 1★ fraud accusations instead. Report 12: five reviewers said the listed support email does not exist; refund and support failures were twice as prevalent in small storefronts, where users are charged and stranded. Report 18: support silence (32, mean 2.72★) landed hardest on payers — a week of silence on a lifetime account with purchase screenshots; the Japanese in-app feedback form rejected every valid e-mail and its text was invisible in dark mode, so Japanese users could only file bugs through the App Store; KakaoTalk was the only Korean channel and closed at weekends; a Canadian found the in-app support link resolved to an ad. Report 20: support went from answering reviews and fixing bugs same-day in 2019–2020 to a dead 'Contact Us' e-mail with an autoresponder and a dormant Instagram account (0.05% → 13.0% of reviews by era); among 148 support-silence reviews the mean was 1.33 versus 3.63 for the 30 who were restored or fixed — the same defect produced either rating depending only on whether anyone answered, worth ~+2.3 stars per recoverable incident. Report 23: support praised (49, 0.67%) with fixes bringing edited upgrades, but genuine silences recur and one reviewer says support implied they don't own an Apple Watch for testing. Report 24: 947 (2.18%, mean 1.528) automated-only support; the refund path works when reached — several 1★ → 4★ edits after a refund — so the failure is reaching it. Report 25: a solo developer answering within a day ('feature requests implemented in less than 24hrs'; 'I can't believe one developer made this') is a purchase trigger — 'After testing the app and interacting with the developer… I've decided to pay without any hesitation' — but support praise thinned 3.0% → 1.6% → 0.9% and one 1★ says the developer 'preferred to argue about what I could see on my end'. Report 26: support unreachable 13 (mean 2.77), support praised 10 (all 5★); support's own advice to reinstall destroyed a paying user's progress and purchase; a premium subscriber's crash went unanswered for months. Report 27: not one review in four years mentions contacting support or a developer reply; the website link in Settings leads to an inactive domain, so the support path is broken — and a solo-developer app with no support channel absorbs an OS-transition break entirely through its public rating. Report 28: 'There is no Support button in the app. Nor on developer's website'; 'no matter how many emails you send, they don't reply'; yet the four who reached the developer got excellent service — a 1★ converted to 5★ after a verification reset 'within an hour… on a Sunday, on a 3 day holiday weekend'; support quality is not the problem, discoverability is — an in-app 'Contact support' and 'Restore purchases' entry point is the cheapest rating intervention available. Report 29: support effectively unreachable — 'I contacted the dev twice but got no response'; a support link that 'takes you to a super-sketch website, circumventing Apple's privacy settings'; with no account and no backup the review page is the only support channel, which is why bugs arrive as public 1★. Report 31: 460 reviews (8.87%, mean 1.32) say support never replied or the contact path was broken (dead typeform links, a Mail-app-only link), rising 0.6% (E1) → 20.3% (E4) → 20.8% (E5); in E1 support was praised (11 of 18 support-praise reviews) — staff a single working contact path with a published response time and resolve by receipt, not by argument. Report 33: support is two-sided — praised 103 (mean 4.73; 'Hana … sent me a video'; 'within one minute') vs support failure 131 (1.70; 5 weeks without reply then the review deleted); English-only replies frustrate Japanese and Chinese users; AI-only support is an emerging negative (8 reviews, 7 in 2025–26: 'Their support is AI'; the chatbot 'stops answering'). Report 34: a single 'Support doesn't respond to emails' in an app whose main asset is a named, responsive solo developer. Report 36: both support-failure records are payers ('contacted the developer twice … I waited too long for a reply and I have now paid. Service matters'; 'a small company and cannot solve problems in mainland China'). Report 41: the only support channel is a mailto: link that dead-ends users without the Mail app ('forcing me to add a mail account'; a trial user 'likely will cancel'), in an app where support closes sales and is the only data-recovery path; support praise collapsed to 1.7% in 2025 as volume tripled, then recovered. Report 42: a paying customer with data loss had no route to a human — 'it says mail isn't connected, but there's no section in the app to connect it' — and replies are canned ('they just reply the same thing to everyone', a 10-vote review). Report 43: support is bimodal because the intake is broken — praised by 24 (mean 4.67; a 2★ raised to 5★ after the exact fix shipped; 'requested a small new feature… added a few days later') vs 7 with no response (mean 1.29, the lowest theme) and 4 reporting the in-app feedback form itself fails ('Feedback email can not send'; 'They have a report bug feature, but that also doesn't work'); 'no response' rose 0.57% → 2.60% by era while praise stayed flat.

title: Family plan
statement: Demand exists (people bought it); report 1's failed only through discoverability (Apple Family Sharing with no in-app affordance). Report 23: Family Sharing is supported on the one-time purchase; a few want to track a child's chores alongside their own inside one account. Report 33: a paid family plan (2025) whose sharing is described as not working (7, mean 2.00).

title: Dates, streaks and statistics correct on every surface — month boundaries, week starts, DST and timezones
statement: Miscounts are ×10.2 over-represented among buyers. Off-by-one dates across app/widget/Watch were report 2's longest-lived bug. Night routines that cross midnight must log to the day they started, honouring a user 'day ends at' setting. Report 23: un-pausing a task marks paused days as missed and resets the streak; a completion 'un-completes' seconds later under sync conflict. Report 25: over-achievement carries into the next day (exceeding a goal pre-completes tomorrow) and logging a bad habit at 200% is rewarded as success (7, 0.53%). Report 29: a month-rollover and weekday-header-offset bug was the dominant defect — 37 reviews (10.11%, mean 2.95 vs 4.73), 78.4% filed on days 28–3 against a 27.6% baseline ('On the last day of every month the app has no idea what day it is… April 30 defaulted to Feb 28'); 62.5% of all 3★; users taught each other to reinstall, which wiped local-only data. Test every date surface at month end, leap day and both week starts. Report 31: time-zone travel rewrote 600- and 1,500-day streaks (13); the week-start setting was ignored and weeks reset on Sunday, including in widgets (30; a 3-year premium user 'begging'); store completions against the local calendar day, not a UTC timestamp.

merged_from.title: Date arithmetic must survive month boundaries and week-start conventions
merged_from.note: C243 (report 29: a month-rollover / weekday-offset bug) is a specific failure of C038's rule, not a separate decision

title: Reminders fire reliably, once
statement: Reminders that work are a top praise item; not firing or spamming is a 1★ driver. Report 23: 97 (1.33%, mean 3.48, 18.6% 1★) — reminders that don't fire (Thailand 4 of 22, 18.2%, limited evidence), fire for already-completed tasks, fire all at once at night, ignore Do Not Disturb, or interrupt a meditation to say meditate; the 'smart' auto-timing algorithm is widely disliked. Report 24: notification volume/control 744 (1.71%, mean 2.437) — users turn all notifications off, which disables the product; give per-notification-type control. Report 27: the reminder fires for a goal already marked complete today — 'a notification that contradicts app state actively trains users to ignore notifications'. Report 28: notification annoyance 5 (0.61%, mean 2.80) — decay-guilt pushes ('YOUR BUNNY'S LOSING HEALTH'). Report 29: reminders that never fire, deleted reminders that keep firing (surviving delete-and-reinstall), and changed times that don't take (6, mean 3.17) — one problem: the notification schedule is written once and never reconciled against the habit's state; cancel scheduled notifications on delete and stop the day's reminders on check-off. Report 30: a user wants an alarm, not just a notification — 'receives an alarm from the app itself and doesn't need another alarm on the phone'. Report 33: reminders praised by 91 (repeat every 30 min until done) and broken in 68, notably when iOS 13 broke notifications. Report 34: the reminder time picker broke for a paying user ('I payed for this app … I might just cancel my membership', Dec 2025) and again Mar 2026; a 2019 buyer got no notifications and returned the purchase. Report 43: an iOS 15 notification regression ran five public weeks (13 Oct – 10 Nov 2021: firing after completion, double notifications, 'I don't think the solution is to have us individually email tech support. It's clearly a bug'; a payer 'over a month and a half… no bug fix'); ghost habits — deleted habits still firing at midnight after reinstall and a new phone (2); notification bugs 15 (2.35%, mean 2.60) on the app's signature feature.

title: Widgets must not go blank, stale or disagree with the app
statement: Broken widget is ×7.8 on 2★. Report 10: the widget rendered as a grey box for five years (117 reviews) — reported mostly by fans, so it never generated pressure. Report 18: the widget went from the top request (31 reviews at 4.77★ before launch) to the top defect surface (214 mentions, 10.45%) — blank, missing from the picker, wrong weekday, false 'all done', check-off opening the app, routine widget rendering to-dos. Report 20: the widget was the top defect surface for five years and the 2★ band's peak theme (13.0%). Report 23: widgets rendering blank or losing configuration (57 explicit widget-bug reviews, mean 3.16; 20 blank/config reports) alongside the interactive-widget regression. Report 25: widget stopped working / not interactive / font fixed (6, 0.46%). Report 27: the widget is the most consistently under-delivering surface and the only one to produce a 1★ on its own ('Widget does and shows absolutely nothing… Just says 0% ALL the time'); 9 gap/defect reviews (6.52%, high-priority) across every one of five years vs 5 praising it. Report 28: no widget at all — 14 requests (1.71%), mean 4.64, zero negative ratings, continuous April 2022 → September 2026, 'i want to be able to click on the widget and shortcut to check a habit as done'; the clearest uncontested gap in the corpus. Report 29: no widget at all — 16 requests (4.37%), the only absent feature with demonstrated substitution (a user on 'Check Me' because it has one) and the one explicit payment offer ('add widget support happy to pay for a lifetime'); three withhold a star for it. Report 30: the Home Screen widget is paywalled and a documented switch followed — 'I downloaded it only for the widget. Turned out it's a paid feature… competitors include it free — I went there'; the widget shown in the store screenshots is not the widget the app provides; the one user who has it is the happiest reviewer. Report 31: widget mentions 195 (3.76%) — positive in E1, demand in E2, complaint after the Oct 2021 downgrade; the widget ignored the week-start setting. Report 34: widget rendering broke with the iOS 18 tinted home screen (white), two of six widgets didn't show days, 'keeps getting disabled' — 5 reviews, 3.0% of E4, one payer 'waste money'.

title: Editing a habit never wipes its history
statement: Multi-year bug; fixing it brought reviewers back to raise their rating. Report 25: archiving or deleting a habit destroys its history (4); preserve history through archive and restore. Report 30: the only way to stop a finished habit is to delete it, which destroys its history.

title: Aim at ADHD / neurodivergent users, students, medication & chronic-illness trackers
statement: Highest-fit, highest-satisfaction audiences (ADHD 7% of US at 4.79; students 4.87). Report 10: 7.36% of 70,041 reviewers self-identify as ADHD/autistic/ND; Australia's base is 11.4%. Report 18: ADHD/ASD/depression/burnout reviewers were the highest-rated audience (36 at 4.53★; 5.95% of US reviews) and the developer put 'ADHD' in the Korean store title — but the same population is most damaged by streak mechanics and excluded by a 9-to-5 onboarding; the positioning ran ahead of the product. Report 23: self-identified ADHD/autism/executive-dysfunction users are a growing, high-satisfaction segment (73, 1.00%, mean 4.45; 0.66% → 0.70% → 1.90% across eras) the app never marketed to; 28 arrived on a therapist/coach/doctor recommendation (mean 4.50); several of them are the strongest capacity complaints because task decomposition is what executive-function support requires, and one calls the help-page wording ableist. Report 24: ADHD/autism/executive-dysfunction users are 933 (2.15%) and grew 30× across eras to 6.01% of 2024–26 reviews — but they are the angriest segment (mean 2.747, 54.2% 1–2★) because the interface overstimulates and the cancel flow exploits executive function; depression/anxiety/PTSD/grief context is 1,256 (2.89%, mean 3.938); clinicians review it and recommend it (24 + 9). Report 25: ADHD/autism/OCD self-identified users are the highest-satisfaction segment (41, 3.13%, mean 4.44, 32 5★; plus 24 at mean 4.67 describing executive difficulty without a diagnosis; three arrive via a clinician including a psychologist recommending it to clients) — and they supply the sharpest paywall anger ('just another app trying to profit off of your disability'); ADHD vocabulary is 4.8× more common in high-spend markets, a diagnosis-prevalence difference not a needs difference. Report 26: ADHD/neurodivergent users (81, 2.11%, mean 3.84 — the lowest of any positively-framed segment) succeed because of simplicity and are hit hardest by the 5-habit cap; mental-health users (32, mean 4.66) are the highest-affect reviews; teens and students (25, ages 10–21, mean 4.16) cannot pay. Report 28: ADHD/autism users (15, mean 4.33) say the reward loop 'works so well for my brain' — and produce the harshest ad verdicts ('whenever I click to complete a habit, it shows me an advert'; 'Bad for ADHD — Has Potential'): interruption cost is not evenly distributed; kids and students are 40 (4.87%), several aged 8–10. Report 31: ADHD / autism / OCD users 33 (mean 4.09 — 'every other app overcomplicates… this app is BEAUTIFUL and simple'), medication and body-care tracking 36 (3.42), mental-health context 38; coaches, clinicians and therapists recommend it — they are the most loyal and the most hurt by regressions (monthly frequency, streak display, medication streaks). Report 33: ADHD, neurodivergent and health users praise the structure ('as an adult with ADHD'; 'I'm neurodivergent and I really hate routine'; medication) and object most clearly to guilt copy and unclosable banners ('I have adhd … huge banner … you CAN NOT CLOSE'). Report 34: ADHD users (5) prefer the simple general tracker — 'apps designed specifically for ADHD … too detailed … This app is simple with just the right amount of detail'; 'MUST. FILL. BOXES.' Report 43: ADHD (18, mean 4.61) and other accessibility accounts (12, 4.75; autism, depression, chronic illness, head injury, ASD, anxiety) are the fastest-growing theme (0.00% → 4.22% → 7.79% by era) and almost entirely US (24 of 25) — 'severe ADHD… complete tasks that would otherwise take hours on end — cooking, cleaning, and even applying makeup'; 'motivated me to shower for the first time in a week'; 'when I don't have the brain power to think it just tells me what to do next'; the mechanics are the multi-step timer and the widget; the listing's 'ADHD-friendly interface' claim is earned without targeting.

title: Flexible / custom frequency
statement: Every X days, specific weekdays, bi-weekly, quarterly, yearly, total-over-a-window — the #1 unmet functional need and highest 4★ lift. Report 12: weekday-only repeats were asked for in Jul 2022 and still missing in May 2026 — three years and ten months. Report 20: frequency was 'N times in M days' only — specific weekdays ('Gym Mon/Wed/Fri') were never expressible in seven years (22 requests) and drove a share of the notification complaints. Report 23: times-per-week, per-day, per-month and every-N-days shipped incrementally; still absent after eleven years — yearly goals, arbitrary intervals (every 6 weeks, quarterly, a shift worker's 4–5-day rotation) and specific dates of the month (101 requests, 1.39%); a non-daily habit also consumes a daily slot under the cap. Report 24: per-weekday / shift-work scheduling requested by 31, 51.6% of them 4–5★. Report 25: flexible scheduling primitives are a stated reason to choose the app — an every-N-days reminder ('the ONLY APP I've found'), N×/week, skip, vacation mode, a custom day-start for shift workers (capped at 11:45); a weekly habit cannot be pinned to a chosen day. Report 26: flexible recurrence ('3× per week') and a vacation/pause mode ('exception periods' while travelling) requested by 12 (0.31%); only per-habit day-of-week scheduling exists. Report 27: flexible weekly frequency shipped ~2025 and is praised ('tasks that can be completed a few times a week rather than everyday'); per-weekday scheduling ('run 1 mile per day during the week, and skip Saturday + Sunday') remains a request; a Monday week-start setting was asked twice in early 2024 and never again.
